results.content: An assistant professor of sociology at Lehman College, City University of New York, Sall’s research examines racialisation through the lived realities of contemporary African migration in the US. “It would be meaningful if African immigrants and their children recognised their stories in my research and felt seen,” she says, adding that amplifying Black immigrant voices is essential to shaping public understanding and policies that affect their lives. She is also an African Research Initiative for Scientific Excellence (ARISE) research fellow at the University of Namibia’s Department of Environmental Sciences, and she runs the Africa Nature Futureslab , supervising three postdoctoral fellows, eight PhD students, four masters students and five interns. Thorn leads the interdisciplinary research programme FLOURISH (Future Landscape Optimisation for peri-Urban Resilience and Ecosystem Health in Africa), which examines how green infrastructure can reduce hydrometeorological risks in informal settlements in Namibia, Madagascar and Sierra Leone, funded by the African Union and European Commission, implemented by the African Academy of Sciences.
